study_identification.title: Multimodal normative modeling in Alzheimer's Disease with introspective variational autoencoders

study_characteristics.study_objective: This study aimed to develop a multimodal soft-introspective VAE (mmSIVAE) for normative modeling in Alzheimer's Disease (AD) to address limitations of VAE-based normative models in accurately modeling healthy control distributions and aggregating multimodal information. The study evaluated whether mmSIVAE with MOPOE aggregation could effectively learn the training distribution of healthy populations, accurately reconstruct inputs, reliably detect outliers, and map latent deviations to feature-space abnormalities in brain regions associated with AD pathology.

deviation_metric.answer: Latent space Mahalanobis distance (D_ml); Feature space Mahalanobis distance (D_mf); Z-scores for latent dimensions (Z_ml); Z-scores for regional feature deviations (Z_mf); Outlier threshold: p < 0.001 for Mahalanobis distance

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Likelihood ratio for outlier detection (comparing outlier rates in disease vs. holdout healthy controls); Pearson correlation between latent deviations (D_ml) and neuropsychological composite scores (memory, executive, language, visual-spatial) - correlations compared using Steiger's Z-test; Linear regression (adjusted for age and sex) between deviation metrics and cognitive composites (β, p-values reported in Table 2); Cohen's d effect sizes for regional Z-score differences between CDR groups and amyloid-negative controls; FDR correction applied for multiple comparisons in regional analyses
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The proposed mmSIVAE with MOPOE aggregation achieved superior reconstruction of healthy controls and highest likelihood ratios for outlier detection (10.2 at d=15) compared to baseline methods, with latent deviations showing significant correlations with cognitive decline and mapping to AD-relevant brain regions.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: mmSIVAE demonstrated the lowest reconstruction errors across all brain regions for both MRI volumes and amyloid SUVR compared to baseline methods (SIVAE, mmVAE, vanilla VAE, mmJSD, JMVAE, MVTCAE). For outlier detection, mmSIVAE with MOPOE achieved the highest likelihood ratio of 10.2 at latent dimension d=15, outperforming all baselines. Latent deviations (D_ml) consistently showed higher likelihood ratios than feature space deviations (D_mf), and MOPOE aggregation outperformed both POE and MOE alone. The model achieved Earth Mover's Distance of 34.043 between control and disease distributions, indicating clear separation. Latent deviations showed significant correlations with cognitive decline: memory (r=-0.573), executive function (r=-0.467), language (r=-0.421), and visual-spatial (r=-0.442), with correlations significantly higher than mmVAE and vanilla VAE baselines (Steiger's Z-test p<0.05). Five latent dimensions (6,7,8,14,15 out of 15) showed statistically significant deviations (|Z_ml|>1.96) and were mapped to feature-space abnormalities. Regional abnormalities showed increased Cohen's d effect sizes across progressive CDR stages, with MRI atrophy most evident in temporal, parietal, and hippocampal regions, and amyloid loading in accumbens, precuneus, frontal and temporal regions, consistent with known AD pathology patterns.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study is limited to cross-sectional analysis without longitudinal validation of deviation trajectories. The normative model was trained on a single dataset (ADNI) which may limit generalizability, though some validation on ADRC is presented in supplementary materials. The study focuses on regional measures rather than voxel-wise analysis, which may miss fine-grained spatial patterns. Model interpretability remains challenging despite efforts to map latent to feature space deviations. The study does not compare against all recent normative modeling approaches such as hierarchical Bayesian regression or Gaussian Process Regression methods. Quality control procedures for the training ADNI cohort are not comprehensively detailed.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study demonstrates technical innovation by extending soft-introspective VAE to multimodal settings with theoretical Nash equilibrium analysis. The MOPOE aggregation approach effectively combines strengths of POE and MOE methods. The framework enables mapping of latent space deviations to interpretable brain regional abnormalities, which is important for clinical applicability. The method shows promise for heterogeneity analysis in AD by identifying individual-level deviation patterns beyond group averages. The supplementary materials indicate broader validation on Knight ADRC dataset with multiple modalities (MRI, amyloid, tau PET), though main paper focuses on two modalities (MRI and amyloid).

general_notes.general_notes: This is a preprint (December 13, 2024) that has not yet undergone peer review. The paper represents a methodological advancement in multimodal normative modeling using introspective VAEs with theoretical contributions. The supplementary materials reference a third modality (tau FTP PET) and additional dataset (Knight ADRC) with 301 CU controls and 129 ADS patients, suggesting broader scope than presented in main paper. The supplementary materials describe a separate mmVAE architecture (SM4.1-4.3) with different specifications (latent dim=64, 4 layers) compared to the main mmSIVAE model (latent dim=5-20, 2 layers), which may indicate different experiments or model versions. The correspondence author is kumarsayantan94@gmail.com. Full list of neuropsychological tests and cognitive composites detailed in SM3. Detailed imaging acquisition and preprocessing protocols for ADRC dataset provided in SM1-SM2.
